thread:
jamie: FYI — scheduling a staged terraform apply tonight (22:00 UTC) for NAT GW replacement + cross-account IAM role update. Plan saved in the runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/natgw-iam-cutover. Deploybot will run canary then serial waves. Provider pin required (see below). Please ack if you can monitor the canary.

rachel: Ack, I can watch the dashboards and take pager for the first 30m. Which metric threshold should we abort on?

jamie: Good. Abort criteria: 1) 5xx rate > 1.5% sustained for 3m, 2) error budget burn > 20% in any 10m window, 3) failed node provisioning > 2 hosts. If hit, abort waves and run rollback play. :rotating_light:

anya: I'll own the canary apply (us-east-1). I'll run preflight smoke: health-checks, e2e short suite, and synthetic traffic for auth flows. I'll post results here.

mateo: I'm backup for Anya and will handle infra alerts. Also added a small sanity eval set for the gateway: 30 requests for common endpoints.

deploybot: deploybot: scheduled apply job created by @jamie for 1716409876. Canary targets: module.network -> natgw-module. Provider pinned: hashicorp/aws 3.4.1. Waves: canary -> wave1 (stagger 2m) -> wave2 (stagger 5m).

oliver: Quick note: before apply, export plan for audit and store with timestamped filename. Example:
```
terraform plan -var-file=prod.tfvars -out=canary.plan
aws s3 cp canary.plan s3://redwood-tf-plans/1716409876-canary.plan
```
Also run `terraform show -json canary.plan > canary.json` for review.

jamie: Provider pin snippet I pushed to the network module:
```hcl
required_providers {
  aws = {
    source  = "hashicorp/aws"
    version = "= 3.4.1"
  }
}
```
Make sure your local modules are updated.

rachel: Rollback steps (short):
1) Abort remaining waves in deploybot.
2) Revert merge commit in git (PR revert).
3) Restore terraform state snapshot from s3 backup created at 21:40 UTC: `s3://redwood-tf-state/backups/network/1716408000.tfstate`
4) Run `terraform init && terraform apply -auto-approve -refresh=false` on the reverted commit (use saved plan if available).
If state restore fails, escalate to oncall infra with the restore playbook.

anya: I'll post canary smoke results here once canary apply completes. If canary passes + no alerts for 15m, proceed with wave1.

devops-bot: Reminder: lock acquired on remote state by jamie for run 1716409876. Lock ID: 9f2a3b. Timeout: 60m.

deploybot: deploybot: canary apply started (us-east-1). Running terraform apply (canary.plan). Logs: https://deploy-logs.internal/1716409876/canary

anya: Canary apply finished — provisioning OK, smoke tests passed (10/10), synthetic auth latency within SLA. No 5xx spikes. Posting test summary.

rachel: All green from dashboards during canary. Proceed with scheduled waves every 10m. I'll keep monitoring. :thumbsup:

jamie: Proceeding to wave1 in 5m. If anyone sees anything weird ping here and run the abort checklist. Thanks everyone.

mateo: Copy — standing by.

deploybot: deploybot: wave1 apply succeeded. wave2 queued, starting in 10m.

oliver: Post-apply checklist reminder: run `terraform state list | grep aws_nat_gateway` and verify tags and routes. Also check peering routes in the routing table.

jamie: Final note — I created a quick lifeboat playbook in the runbook section for emergency manual rollback (steps to force restore state snapshot + drain). Link in root runbook.

devops-bot: Lock released for run 1716409876.

rachel: Great run. Will follow up with a short postmortem + release notes entry tomorrow.

jamie: Thanks all. :)
